items.title: Who Actually Made This? The Question AI Is Forcing Music to Ask.
items.excerpt: Op-ed arguing AI can support music creation, but transparency about the degree of human involvement is essential to preserving the artist-fan connection.

items.title: Olivia Rodrigo Clarifies AI Stance Following 'Invasive' Tech Investor Dating Rumors: 'Absolutely No'
items.excerpt: Olivia Rodrigo clarified she does not use AI in her music and addressed rumors linking her to an AI tech investor.

items.title: RIAA CEO Talks Midterms, AI Deepfakes and Trump: 'Music Is a Very Bipartisan Issue'
items.excerpt: On Billboard's On the Record, RIAA CEO Mitch Glazier compares Napster with AI and explains why he is confident the NO FAKES Act on voice/likeness deepfakes will pass.

items.title: Suno Hires Ticketmaster Executive to Lead New Live Experiences Division
items.excerpt: Suno launches a Live Experiences division (including Songkick) led by ex-Ticketmaster EVP Michael Chua, with an initial focus on integrating Songkick into the AI music platform. Note: framed as exec hire; product angle is Suno moving into live.

items.title: Fender revamps its website with AI tool and more artist content
items.excerpt: Fender relaunches its website with a new AI-powered tool for players alongside expanded artist content, extending its push beyond instruments into apps and education.

items.title: Google launches AI-powered 'experimental gaming' platform Playground
items.excerpt: Google's new AI game-creation platform Playground folds in its generative models, including its flagship AI music model; Music Ally frames it alongside the music industry's own AI debate. Music angle is secondary.

items.title: Google picks Base for Music for its Gemini Startup Forum, as French company says it uses AI to predict music marketing ROI
items.excerpt: French startup Base for Music, which uses AI to predict the ROI of music marketing campaigns, was selected for Google's Gemini Startup Forum from 2,000+ applicants.

items.title: A US appeals court has rejected a 'fair use' defense over AI training. What does it mean for the labels' fight with Suno?
items.excerpt: MBW Explains: what the appeals ruling for Thomson Reuters against ROSS Intelligence means for the major labels' copyright case against AI music generator Suno. Note: underlying ruling already covered; this is the Suno-specific follow-up.

items.title: Fred again.. on AI-generated music: 'I'm not worried about the threat of AI'
items.excerpt: Fred again.. says he has felt 'no pull whatsoever' to use AI in his production process and is not worried about AI-generated music as a threat. (Date from body text: 28 September 2026; time unknown, set to noon UTC.)

items.title: '스님부터 80대 창작자까지'... 노이즈 홍종구, AI 음악 최초 플랫폼 '아뮤차트'로 판 깔았다 [IS인터뷰]
items.excerpt: Former NOISE member Hong Jong-gu launches 'Amuchart', billed as the first platform dedicated to AI music, and plans to have well-received AI songs re-recorded by real singers as a management business.

items.title: [K팝과 AI 혁명] '지휘자'가 된 창작자들, 대체할 수 없는 것들을 향하여
items.excerpt: Closing installment of Ilgan Sports' K-pop and AI series: as generative AI shakes up K-pop production, creators are becoming 'conductors' directing AI while focusing on what cannot be replaced.

items.title: Mastering The Mix releases CARBON Q connected EQ for $56
items.excerpt: CARBON Q is an 11-band connected EQ that locally separates a reference track into vocals, music, drums and bass, then turns their tonal/level relationships into a session-wide preset. Note: article does not say 'AI'; relevance is the stem-separation-driven mix workflow. Date only (no time).

items.title: MOTU Digital Performer 12 now available
items.excerpt: Digital Performer 12 adds AI-powered stem separation (drums, bass, vocals, guitar plus ensemble strings and brass) and Dolby Atmos support to MOTU's DAW.

items.title: Watch what Herbie Hancock had to say about technology in 1984
items.excerpt: CDM revisits a 1984 film of Herbie Hancock jamming with Quincy Jones on the Fairlight, reading his approach to machines as a lesson for the AI era: what makes you smarter is not AI or a new plug-in.
